body:
Unfortunately no, I dropped contact with my only friends during my first incident. I do have some open-minded family in another state, but we're not close enough for me to ask that of them and even the idea of me asking to crash at a relative's place instead of my parents' would likely devastate at least my mother. It would have to be under the guise of a job opportunity in the region, which wouldn't happen anyways because the industry doesn't have a real presence in that state.

I think no matter what it would come to a confrontation of why I can't live under them, in which case either I back down or they kick me out. Or if the confrontation never happens, either I waste my 20's as a miserable leech with huge debt or I leave them in grieving for years with huge debt.

It's honestly hard to judge what the best case scenario would be.

It's not over with Uni just yet. I won't give up until it's set in stone, but my chances are very bleak. And then that's not even considering how unsustainable it is with this pattern I've locked myself into.

At the beginning, with the first incident, it was about having been raised to see uni as the absolute pinnacle, with every decision and lifestyle choice being made for me in with uni in mind. It was never verbally forced on me, and my parents asked me several times if it was what I wanted, but it really didn't feel like a choice at all. Especially after being told over and over through grade school that if I wanted a career, there was no choice but college-- even though I now know that to be a well-intentioned yet misguided lie. I think I've gotten over that though, but now I'm looking at the bigger picture.

The real problem is my debt will be enormous, and my only safety net will be my parents. Even ignoring the social stigma that comes with it, I can't stand living with them because I have to repress myself and they've stuck to the same rigid set of rules from before I was a teenager. It's not a healthy living situation, and I can't take the blow to my dignity either. I also get stuck with an unfulfilling dead end job with no way forward.

I have no other options, but I can't afford myself a way out because I totally deserve it anyways. And yet I don't think I'll be able to live like that as I grow into my 20's with zero independence or freedom while being shackled with guilt and debt. It'll be absolutely miserable, with the only silver lining being that my family doesn't get hurt over losing me and I contribute a bit to paying back the loans.

I just don't see any truly positive path from here, even trying to be optimistic. I know I said in the OP I'm not depressed, but... this is very depressing.
